findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt:1145 isTrasladoDeliveryOk does not verify the service type
findings.claim: The TRASLADO filter gate checks only the delivery address (Cruz Verde contains or SavedLocationManager match) and never the servicio field, by explicit product decision because Picap renders every Traslado as Mostrador. Consequence: an OMS order whose delivery address matches a saved location would also be accepted while the Traslado filter is active. The user accepted this trade-off when specifying the rule.

findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/OrderHistoryManager.kt:47 addOrder deduplicates by id and never refreshes
findings.claim: If Picap re-parses the same order id with updated fields (for example a changed ganancia), addOrder skips it and the carousel keeps the first-seen snapshot, while the live card shows the updated values via setOrder. Divergence is limited to display; auto-accept always evaluates the fresh parse.
proof_refs: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/OrderHistoryManager.kt:47 addOrder returns early when the id already exists

findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/OrderHistoryManager.kt:47 unbounded history rewritten as one JSON blob per capture
findings.claim: History is intentionally unbounded until app data is cleared; every new order rewrites the full JSON array on the main thread. With thousands of stored orders this adds a periodic hitch at capture time. Acceptable at realistic volumes per the maintainer decision, but a size cap or background write would remove the risk if the list grows very large.
proof_refs: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/OrderHistoryManager.kt:47 persist rewrites the full list on each add

findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MainActivity.kt:607 pager snaps to newest whenever history grows
findings.claim: The LaunchedEffect jumps to the newest page on every history insertion, so a user browsing older orders is moved back to the newest when a new order arrives. This favors live-order visibility over browsing position and was a deliberate choice; deleting pages does not trigger the jump and clamps to the last valid index instead.
